summary: Adversarial review of the solution-architect's SDD (tasks/agent-outputs/solution-architect/FEAT-5.json) against the live code in backend/src/masterDataRouter.js, masterDataSchema.js, masterDataTables.js and migrations 0011/0012. Found one Critical, pipeline-halting defect the SDD did not surface: the SDD's migration design drops resource_cost.name, but the shared list query used by every master-data table (including resource_cost) is hardcoded to `order by (deleted_at is not null), name asc` in masterDataRouter.js's GET / handler. Dropping the column without changing that query breaks GET /v1/resource-cost (and the MCP tools/frontend table that read it) with a Postgres 'column name does not exist' error on every list request. This is a real regression in the shared factory, not just resource_cost-local, and must be resolved in the SDD/System-Engineer design before any code is written. Also flagged one Important (non-blocking) correctness gap in the lookup-join design, and resolved the three open items the SDD explicitly deferred to this stage. No files beyond this report were created or edited — this is a read-only review stage; the migration was not written or applied.

findings.title: Dropping resource_cost.name breaks the shared GET / list query's hardcoded ORDER BY
findings.detail: backend/src/masterDataRouter.js line 44: `select * from ${tableName} order by (deleted_at is not null), name asc limit $1 offset $2` is the one generic list query used by createMasterDataRouter(table) for all 9 master-data tables, resource_cost included. It assumes every table has a `name` column. The SDD's migration_design_for_system_engineer explicitly plans `alter table public.resource_cost drop column name` (dropping the placeholder name field, superseded by employeeId), with no corresponding change to this ORDER BY. Once applied, every `GET /v1/resource-cost` (list) call — used by the frontend dashboard's read-only table view and indirectly exercised by the MCP server's own read paths — will fail with a raw Postgres 'column "name" does not exist' error surfaced as an unhandled 500, i.e. the entire Resource Cost table becomes unreadable via the list endpoint the moment the migration lands. GET /v1/resource-cost/:id is unaffected (no ORDER BY there), so this would likely pass a shallow single-row smoke test while breaking the primary list view.
findings.verification: Confirmed by direct Read of backend/src/masterDataRouter.js (not trusted from any prior stage's summary — none of the prior stages quoted this line or the ORDER BY clause at all) and cross-checked that resource_cost's only current column beyond the shared shape is `name` (backend/migrations/0011_create_additional_master_data_tables.sql), and that no `sortColumn`/`orderBy` override exists anywhere in backend/src/masterDataTables.js's field-descriptor shape.
findings.required_resolution: Before Developer/Engineer stages write code: the shared router needs a table-level sort override (e.g. `table.sortColumn ?? 'name'`, falling back to an always-present column such as `created_at` or `id` when a table has no `name`), OR the migration must not fully drop `name` (e.g. keep a computed/derived non-null placeholder), OR resource_cost's list ordering is special-cased. Given CLAUDE.md's Simplicity-First and the existing `hasCode`-style per-table override precedent, a generic `sortColumn` field-descriptor property (defaulting to `'name'` so the other 8 tables are untouched) is the minimal, convention-consistent fix — this should be folded into the SDD's already-planned lookups/validateExists descriptor work rather than left as an implementation-time surprise. This must be decided at this design stage, not discovered by the Tester, because it changes the migration's own shape (whether name is dropped at all) and the field-descriptor shape (whether a new key is needed) — both design-stage concerns per CLAUDE.md §7.4.

findings.title: Lookup JOIN condition as specified doesn't match the SDD's own stated soft-delete-null behavior
findings.detail: The SDD's `lookup.read_path_change` says: 'a resource_cost row whose employeeId matches no resource... must still be listed... employeeName/employeeDesignation simply come back null in that edge case' for a resource later soft-deleted. But the join it specifies is `left join ${lookups.table} j on j.${lookups.on} = t.${lookups.on}` — with no `and j.deleted_at is null` condition. A soft-deleted resource still exists as a row (deleted_at set, not removed), so this join would still match it and return its stale name/designation, not null, directly contradicting the SDD's stated intent. This doesn't block the pipeline (it's a one-clause fix: `on j.${lookups.on} = t.${lookups.on} and j.deleted_at is null`), but it must be corrected in the System Engineer/Developer stage's actual query, not just described optimistically in prose.
findings.verification: Read directly from the SDD JSON's own `lookup.read_path_change` field; no code exists yet to cross-check against (lookups aren't implemented), so this is a design-consistency finding, not a code finding.

open_items_resolved.left_join_vs_inner_join: Confirmed correct as designed: LEFT JOIN is required so a resource_cost row survives even when its employeeId no longer resolves (soft-deleted or, in a future scenario, hard-deleted resource). Not blocking, but see the Important finding above — the join's null-on-soft-delete behavior needs an explicit `deleted_at is null` predicate to actually deliver what the SDD claims.
open_items_resolved.drop_name_outright_vs_two_phase_migratio: Acceptable in principle per database.md's own stated rationale (the two-phase rule protects readers of live data; an empty placeholder table has none) — but this determination must be based on an actual row-count check against the live Supabase resource_cost table at migration-authoring time, not assumed. This is unchanged from the SDD's own position; adding only that the drop-column change is what makes the Critical ORDER BY finding above trigger, so whoever authors migration 0013 must fix the ORDER BY issue in the same change set that drops `name`, not as a follow-up.
open_items_resolved.422_validation_error_shape_for_bad_emplo: Confirmed correct: reusing the existing generic `validation_error` code with a per-field `details.employeeId` message is consistent with api.md and with how every other required-field validation failure is already reported in this codebase (masterDataSchema.js's validateBody uses the same details-keyed-by-field shape). No need for a bespoke `employee_not_found` code — inventing one would be an unjustified deviation from the existing single validation-error convention this file already uses everywhere else.

non_findings_explicitly_checked: validateExists soft-delete semantics (deleted_at is null in the existence check) — correctly specified, consistent with PATCH/DELETE already refusing soft-deleted rows.

Generalization of validateExists/lookups by table/column rather than hardcoded to resource_cost/resources — confirmed genuinely reusable for resource_deployment later, not over-engineered given tech-lead's explicit reuse rationale; this is proportionate abstraction, not gold-plating.
employee_id column type match (integer on both sides, migration 0012's resources.employee_id is `integer not null` with a unique constraint) — FK and join are type-compatible, no casts needed.

MCP layer staying thin / single enforcement point in the backend — verified against mcp-server/src/masterDataTables.js and the tech-lead's own apiClient.js check; no bespoke MCP-side validation is introduced, consistent with the stated single-enforcement-point design.

Frontend labeling convention ('Employee <Field>') — verified against the live src/lib/masterDataApi.js Resources entry (FEAT-6, commit 5b1f29b already applied) for consistency; the SDD's proposed resource-cost columns[] match the pattern exactly, including employeeId not getting a double 'Employee' prefix.

Other 8 master-data tables' read/write paths remaining untouched by the new `validateExists`/`lookups` descriptors, since both are additive and gated by field/table-level presence checks — confirmed structurally sound as designed (the only place this breaks down is the Critical ORDER BY finding above, which is a pre-existing hardcoding the SDD's migration exposes, not something the new descriptors themselves cause).
migration_status: Not written to disk. Not applied via mcp__Supabase__apply_migration. Per CLAUDE.md §7.6 Invariant 2 and this role's own blocking-finding mandate, migration authorship should not proceed until the ORDER BY / sortColumn question above is folded into the design.
